content:
julia: Quick sync — post-RFC followup on the concatenation/merge semantics for mixed-precision checkpoints. I want an ops-safe design we can implement before the next Dedicated rollout.
kevin: Short answer: exposing a blind `merge` primitive is dangerous. We hit a headwise bitpack mismatch last month that caused ~4% quality drift in a small eval.
sophia: Agreed. We need a compatibility invariant. Either require identical pack layouts or define a clear, measurable upconvert path.
maria: For many customers the cost of an occasional upconvert is fine; on our p4d bench upconvert 4->8 adds ~+1.8ms/token median, but it preserved perplexity.
ajay: Could we refuse merging at runtime and force a `reconcile()` API that does explicit conversion? That avoids silent regressions.
julia: Proposal sketch:
1) Fast path: profiles identical (bitwidth + pack_kind + head_stride) -> memcopy concat.
2) Reshape path: same bitwidth but different pack_kind -> pack-reshape, slower but preserves quant semantics.
3) Upconvert path: differing bitwidths -> upconvert to int8 or fp16 per policy.
4) Refuse path: if structural mismatch (embed dim/head count) -> fail with clear error + telemetry.
kevin: Pack-reshape can cause big memory churn and pauses if done synchronously. Suggest: do an async in-place reshape when possible, otherwise stall request with a short backpressure window.
sophia: Ops-bot note: queued a perf job to measure reshape cost across our most common pack kinds.
ops-bot: perf job created: https://ci.redwood/profiles/pack-reshape/12345 — status: queued
maria: KV cache stability: if we change layout mid-conversation we must preserve token offsets and key ordering. Any reconcile must produce an identical logical key sequence.
ajay: Implementation idea: add a compact header to stored quant blobs: `bitwidth|pack_kind|head_stride|pad`. Runtime uses header to decide which path. Header is tiny (single byte flags + 3 bytes).
julia: Good. API rule: profiles saved to model registry must include canonical header; runtime refuses merge if headers conflict unless `reconcile=true` is explicit.
kevin: Testing: add litmus tests that simulate mid-conversation profile swaps. Measure tail latency and quality deltas. Also add regression harness that injects single-layer pack differences.
sophia: Telemetry: emit `quant.merge.path` values: `identical`, `reshape`, `upconvert`, `refused` and `reconcile_async`. Track p90 tail latency per value.
maria: Edge-case: per-layer mixed quant (layerA 4-bit, layerB fp8) within the same checkpoint. Merging two checkpoints with different per-layer layouts is trappy. We should default to refuse unless operator explicitly opts into `allow_mixed_profile_merges=true` at deploy time.
ajay: Ops should have a Console toggle that displays a warning and a sample-quality delta estimate if they enable `allow_mixed_profile_merges`.
julia: Operational gates: canary criteria = <=1% relative quality regression on canonical eval sets, and median latency delta <=+3ms for hotpath. If either fails, rollback.
kevin: I'll take the PR that defines the header bytes layout + reconcile pseudocode + pack-reshape algorithm.
sophia: I'll build the microbench harness and add the telemetry hooks.
maria: I'll draft Console UX language for the `allow_mixed_profile_merges` opt-in and the warning banner.
ajay: Also add an ops runbook snippet: when `quant.merge.path=refused` escalate to ML infra with the `reconcile` request id.
julia: Thanks. If no objections I'll create the GH issues for the PR, perf job, tests, console flag, and runbook by EOD. :thumbsup:
kevin: No objections. pinging @sophia for the perf bits.
sophia: On it, will start tomorrow morning and post initial numbers here.
julia: Great — closing this sync for now.
